item.title: Sexual equality: motion on gender identity rejected
item.description: The Council of States rejected, by 25 votes to 19, the motion to extend the Gender Equality Act to cases involving sexual orientation and gender identity.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Council of States rejected the motion by 25 votes to 19. - The request concerned sexual orientation and gender identity. - The two organizations criticize the decision by the Council of States. - The organizations announce a renewed commitment in workplaces.
## Key facts - Decision → rejected by the Council of States - Vote → 25 votes to 19 - Request → extend the protection of the Gender Equality Act - Scope → discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity - Organizations → Gruppo Donne USS Ticino e Moesa, Imbarco Immediato - Location → Bellinzona
In Bellinzona, the Gruppo Donne of the Swiss Trade Union Federation Ticino and Moesa and the Association Imbarco Immediato reacted to the decision by the Council of States to reject the motion calling for the protection of the Gender Equality Act to be explicitly extended to discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
The motion was rejected by 25 votes to 19. The two organizations describe this as “profoundly disappointing” and argue that, under current legislation, people who experience discrimination at work because of their sexual orientation or gender identity do not benefit from the same protection provided by the Gender Equality Act.
### Consequences identified by the organizations
According to the statement, this gap can affect access to employment, employment conditions, career prospects and dignity in the workplace. During the parliamentary debate, add Gruppo Donne USS Ticino e Moesa and Imbarco Immediato, the existence of discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity was acknowledged. In their view, however, Parliament chose not to close this legislative gap.
The organizations also dispute the idea that protection against discrimination can be limited to traditionally recognized categories. “The fight against gender discrimination cannot therefore stop at the boundaries of a binary conception of gender,” they state.
In the statement, the failure to give the green light is described as “a missed opportunity” to bring legislation into line with the reality of the world of work and society. It also recalls that the Social Security and Health Committee of the Council of States had acknowledged that including sexual orientation in the Gender Equality Act would have made it possible to put into practice, in employment relationships, protection already recognized by the Federal Constitution.
> “There is no real equality if some people are left outside the protection of the law.”
Finally, the two organizations announce that they will continue their efforts in workplaces, in collective agreements, in collective bargaining and at the political level. ## What changes for the world of work
The decision described in the source leaves open the issue raised by the two organizations: the protection provided by the Gender Equality Act, in their view, does not apply in the same way to discrimination related to sexual orientation and gender identity. The practical issue therefore concerns the employment relationship at several stages, from access to employment through career development and dignity in the workplace.
The issue is not limited to the possibility of obtaining a job. The organizations also mention employment conditions and career development, together with dignity in the workplace. The gap described in the statement therefore spans several stages of the professional relationship, as listed by the associations and trade unions.
### Two levels of protection invoked in the debate
The discussion arising from the decision can be viewed on two levels. On the one hand, there is the protection already provided by the Gender Equality Act for traditionally recognized categories. On the other, there is a demand to make protection for sexual orientation and gender identity explicit. The motion was specifically intended to fill this gap in the legislation.
The Social Security and Health Committee of the Council of States, the source recalls, had recognized that including sexual orientation in the Gender Equality Act would have given concrete effect, in employment relationships, to protection already recognized by the Federal Constitution. Parliament instead rejected the motion. For Gruppo Donne USS Ticino e Moesa and Imbarco Immediato, this choice fails to bring legislation into line with the reality of the world of work and society.
The protection, the organizations argue, should not depend «on whom one loves or how one lives one’s identity». Their criticism therefore also concerns the criterion used to define equality: if some people remain outside the protection of the law, equality is not complete.
The source indicates that the issue will continue to be addressed in workplaces, collective agreements, collective bargaining and at the political level. Trade unions and professional associations intend to act in these areas to create tools that guarantee the same rights and the same dignity. To follow the issue of work in Switzerland, annunci di lavoro and information on busta paga svizzera can be consulted.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## The next initiatives indicated
The statement from the two organizations indicates the areas in which their commitment will continue: workplaces, collective agreements, bargaining and the political sphere. According to the source, these are the areas in which trade unions and trade associations intend to build tools capable of guaranteeing the same rights and the same dignity.
To follow the announced line, the reader can focus on these four areas. The first is the workplace, where the issue is brought back to professional relationships. The second concerns collective agreements. The third is bargaining, indicated separately in the statement. The fourth is the political sphere, in which the organizations intend to continue taking action after the motion was rejected.
### Mobilization on multiple fronts
The announced strategy is not limited to a single level. Work, collective agreements, bargaining and politics are presented together as the areas in which to achieve full protection against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
This means that the declared commitment does not end with the decision of the Council of States. Gruppo Donne USS Ticino e Moesa and Imbarco Immediato assure that they will continue their work to obtain protection without exceptions and without blind spots. Their action is therefore positioned simultaneously within employment relationships, collective instruments and political debate.
The final message from the two organizations is clear: «An equality law must protect all people who experience discrimination, without exceptions and without blind spots». The request is thus transferred from the parliamentary vote to the places where, according to the statement, trade unions and trade associations can build tools to guarantee the same rights and the same dignity.

item.title: Eni cuts fuel, domino effect uncertain in Switzerland
item.description: Eni sets a price cap at 2,19 €/l for diesel and 1,99 €/l for petrol (2,05 CHF and 1,88 CHF) for one month, with a possible extension until the end of the year; 30 Enilive stations in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Eni cuts petrol and diesel starting Monday 28 September - Cap: 2,19 euros/litre for diesel, 1,99 for petrol - Price cap valid for one month, possible extension until year-end - 30 Enilive stations in Ticino, Swiss extension uncertain
## Key facts
- What → Eni price cap on petrol and diesel - Prices → 2,19 euros/litre for diesel; 1,99 euros/litre for petrol - Amounts in CHF → 2,05 for diesel; 1,88 for petrol - Duration → one month, possible extension until year-end - Average saving → 9,35 euros for diesel; 8,45 euros for petrol on the regular network - Switzerland → 30 Enilive stations in Canton Ticino
On Monday 28 September, in Rome, Eni launched discounts on petrol and diesel. The price cap sets diesel at 2,19 euros per litre, equivalent to 2,05 Swiss francs, and unleaded petrol at 1,99 euros, equivalent to 1,88 francs. The stated reduction is around 17 cents compared with current average levels.
The cap will remain in effect for one month, with the possibility of an extension until the end of the year. Eni presented it as a new contribution of solidarity to the country, consumers and its own customers. The Italian government thanked the company, linking the decision to the need to curb high fuel prices which, because of the difficult international context, are affecting families.
The decision has already prompted a first reaction. Socar, an Azerbaijani energy company that acquired Italiana Petroli from Api Holding last May, announced a limit on petrol and diesel selling prices across its network. The discounts will start at IP stations and will then be extended to Esso stations. Experts, however, still consider the spread of the measures among other operators uncertain and point to the presence of obstacles.
### Differences between the initiatives
The two initiatives do not coincide. IP has not set, at least for now, a price cap with precise values: it has committed to containing prices, also defining them based on the sustainability of the entire supply chain. One possibility is the initial involvement of IPmatic stations, which are fully automated and have no attendant, but the methods and timing have not been made official. Eni's mechanism appears broader and could involve Esso stations and other operators that purchase fuel from IP to market it under different brands.
The response for Switzerland remains open. It is not yet possible to know whether the measure will reach Enilive and Socar's Swiss network. Enilive Suisse, which operates 30 filling stations in Canton Ticino alone, has been contacted but has not yet replied. The source indicates that lowering prices in the border area should not be enough to trigger a real rush by people from Ticino to fill up in the provinces of Como and Varese. The situation may be reassessed in the coming days. ## What changes for those who refuel in Ticino
For those who live in Ticino, the operational fact is not yet a new Swiss price, but the uncertain scope of the Italian announcement. The values in euros and Adusbef's estimates describe the network affected by the Italian measures: they do not authorize considering 2,19 euros for diesel or 1,99 for petrol as prices automatically applicable to an Enilive station in Switzerland. The distinction is crucial for assessing the cost of living without turning an announcement into savings that are already available.
### Three scenarios to distinguish
| Scenario | What is known | Practical interpretation | | Eni in Italy | Precise cap and defined duration | The figure does not confirm a price for Switzerland | | Enilive and Socar in Ticino | Possible extension, but no response from Enilive Suisse | Prices and timing remain to be verified | | IP and Esso | IP launch and subsequent Esso extension announced by Socar | The domino effect remains possible, but not certain |
The first useful comparison concerns the route taken. Adusbef calculates an average saving of 9,35 euros on a full tank of diesel and 8,45 euros on a full tank of petrol on the ordinary road network; on motorways, the situation is different. For a Ticinese user, therefore, the figure is not a universal amount: it depends on the fuel and the type of network, as well as on whether it is applied in Switzerland. The source does not provide an equivalent amount for Ticino stations. The comparison between the figures in euros and the values expressed in francs can be followed using comparatore CHF/EUR, without confusing currency conversion with the extension of the discount.
The IP model also deserves attention. Since no numerical cap has yet been set, the containment would depend on the sustainability of the entire supply chain; the possible involvement of IPmatic adds an operational hypothesis, not a certain date. For families following costo della vita in Svizzera, the point to measure therefore remains the actual price at the pump in Ticino. The simple Italian announcement, on its own, does not yet indicate how much will be saved in Switzerland.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to assess the impact over the next few days
The situation can be reassessed over the next few days, as the source indicates. To avoid confusing Italian announcements with a measure already operational in Switzerland, it is advisable to follow five steps.
### A five-step check
1. Separate the date and territory. Monday 28 September is the start date of the Eni discount announced for the Italian network. It should not be read as automatic confirmation for the Swiss network.
2. Identify the fuel. Diesel and petrol have different caps: 2,19 euro and 1,99 euro per litre, with the equivalents in francs indicated by the source. The comparison must be made on the product actually purchased.
3. Distinguish the network. For savings estimates, Adusbef refers to the ordinary road network and treats the case of motorways separately. A calculation referring to the former should not be transferred to the latter.
4. Verify any extension to Ticino. Enilive Suisse operates 30 stations in Canton Ticino, but no response has arrived on whether the measure also applies there. As long as this point remains open, the Italian price cap is not a guarantee for a Swiss distributor.
5. Follow the domino schedule. Socar indicated a start at IP stations and a subsequent extension to Esso; for IP, however, the arrangements and timing have not been made official. The situation must therefore be updated when indications emerge regarding the networks involved.
This sequence makes it possible to use the available figures without turning them into promises. The source does not announce a rush by people from Ticino to fill up in Como and Varese: it says that the reduction in the border area should not be sufficient, but leaves open a new assessment. The practical figure to monitor will therefore be the actual price charged, not just the cap announced in Italy.
To relate a change in costs to the family budget, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Paediatric first aid: mandatory training request
item.description: In 2025, 296 interventions involving children up to 6 years old were recorded. The motion calls for certified, two-year training.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2025, 296 interventions involving children under 6 were recorded - The motion calls for mandatory pediatric training every two years - The lead signatory is Simona Genini, with eight co-signatories - The scope includes nurseries, holiday camps and services overseen by the Canton
## Key facts - Location → Bellinzona - Lead signatory → Simona Genini, member of parliament and PLR deputy group leader - Interventions in 2025 → 296 - Causes indicated → 65 seizures; 52 febrile or infectious conditions without shock; 50 traumatic brain injuries; 42 respiratory disorders or insufficiencies - Proposed update → certified training, in principle at least every two years
In 2025, 296 interventions involving children under 6 were recorded in Ticino. Almost one a day, according to the data cited in the motion submitted to the Council of State in Bellinzona.
The lead signatory is Simona Genini, member of parliament and PLR deputy group leader. She is joined by eight co-signatories. The request is to make pediatric first-aid training mandatory and update it periodically for anyone whose professional activity involves directly caring for children.
### The request to the Council of State
The signatories emphasize that children’s safety depends not only on the premises, internal procedures or the possibility of calling 144. It is also necessary to know what to do during the time that passes before emergency services arrive. They cite choking, loss of consciousness, seizures, severe allergic reactions and accidents in water. They argue that the person present with the child is necessarily the first to intervene.
> «When it comes to children’s safety, it is not enough merely to take care of the premises, internal procedures or the possibility of calling 144».
The data indicated in the motion include 65 seizures, 52 febrile or infectious conditions without shock, 50 traumatic brain injuries and 42 respiratory disorders or insufficiencies. Almost one third of the interventions took place outside the home. The text specifies, however, that these figures do not say in how many cases the child was in the care of a facility or professional.
The proposal concerns staff with direct responsibility for caring for children at asilo nido and micro-nurseries, daycare families, extracurricular centers, socialization centers, holiday camps, organized stays and other services subject to cantonal authorization, recognition or oversight. The Government should also assess whether to include nannies and babysitters when they work professionally or regularly and for pay, while excluding occasional services.
According to the signatories, the provisions currently in force in Ticino do not establish a general and uniform obligation for all people directly responsible for children. For this reason, the motion calls for certified, predominantly practical training, with refresher training in principle at least every two years and recognition of certificates already obtained if they meet the requirements. ## What would change in practice Today, according to the proposers, in Ticino there is no general and uniform obligation that requires all people with direct custody to have certified and updated training. The requested novelty is therefore not an additional course for a single role, but a requirement referring to the staff who directly assume care in the listed services.
### A requirement distributed across the service The motion considers insufficient the idea that having a single trained person per structure is enough. That person may be absent, on break, engaged with another group, or not present during an outing. The coverage envisioned by the signatories therefore follows the direct care responsibility, not just the existence of a certificate within the organization.
Comparing with other cantons shows that the request does not indicate a single model. In Bern, certain categories of staff must possess pediatric first aid knowledge and update it at least every two years. In Geneva, the educational staff of early childhood facilities must be able to provide first aid and keep BLS-AED-SRC training updated every two years. The motion also references the models of Fribourg and Lucerne, without attributing the same operational detail in the text.
For Ticino, the proposed criterion is certified but mainly practical training, without assigning exclusivity to a particular course or body. The practical part and specific emergencies should be adapted to the different age groups. The update would, in principle, be at least biennial. Certificates already obtained would not be automatically excluded: they would be recognized if they ensured the minimum content and practical component required.
### The limit of available data The 296 interventions of 2025 show the volume of pediatric rescue interventions cited in the text, but do not allow converting the data into a statistic on infant care facilities. The motion states this explicitly. Therefore, one cannot, based solely on those figures, determine how many emergencies involved nurseries, day families, colonies or other services.
The possible extension to grandparents and babysitters remains a judgment requested from the Government: it would concern professional or regular paid activity, not occasional. For facilities and services, the possible operational shift would also depend on inserting the requirement into existing cantonal procedures, the transitional period for those already in operation, and the financing methods for the first training and updates, including possible participation of the Canton. Those looking for opportunities in the sector can consult the job postings, keeping the training proposal distinct from the process still required by the State Council.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to prepare for the potential application
The motion requests the State Council to introduce the requirement and incorporate it into existing cantonal procedures. For those working or managing a service, the text allows identifying some preparatory steps and presents concrete indications.
### A five-step verification
1. Map responsibilities. The first verification concerns who has direct responsibility for care in nurseries and micro-nurseries, family day cares, extracurricular and socialization centers, colonies, organized stays, and other authorized, recognized or cantonally supervised services. It is not simply being present in the facility that defines the scope: the motion refers to direct care.
2. Check certifications. The proposal does not ask to cancel already completed training. It asks to recognize them when they guarantee minimum content and practical components. The verification should therefore focus on what the certificate covers and the practical part, without assuming that a certification will be automatically accepted.
3. Plan updates. The indicated reference is at least every two years. The training should remain predominantly practical and adapt the operational part and emergencies to different age groups. The motion does not bind the choice to a specific course or organization.
4. Separate regular and occasional activities. For nannies and babysitters, the Government is called to evaluate an extension only when the activity is professional or regular and paid. Occasional services are excluded from the indicated requirement.
5. Follow transition and costs. The text requests a transitional period for personnel already active and an evaluation on how to finance initial training and updates, including possible cantonal participation. Their definition will have to be inserted into cantonal procedures.
This reading allows distinguishing what is already written in the proposal from what will need to be defined. Minimum contents are already indicated: airway clearance, pediatric resuscitation, defibrillator when indicated, water accidents, convulsions, allergic reactions, hemorrhages, traumas, burns and poisonings. What remains to be specified are procedural integration, methods of recognizing certifications and funding.
For those evaluating employment in care, following the motion's process helps to understand if and how the requirement will enter services subject to authorization, recognition or cantonal supervision. To complete the personal comparison, consult the salary calculator.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - More than 170 states approved the draft Framework. - The decision was postponed again: attention is now focused on December. - Accelleron and Burckhardt Compression are feeling the pressure. - ABB reports that customer activity is normal.
## Key facts - Objective → net-zero emissions by 2050 - First approval → April 2025 - Expected rules → large ships from 2027 - First postponement → October 2025 - New postponement → December - Estimated emissions → approximately 2-3% of global CO2 emissions
### The international decision
In April 2025, the more than 170 member states of the International Maritime Organization, including Switzerland, had approved the draft of a «Net-Zero Framework». The project aims to reduce the international maritime transport sector's net greenhouse gas emissions to zero by 2050. It also provides for a kind of CO2 tax on vessels and rules intended to apply to large ships from 2027.
Global shipping remains largely dependent on heavy fuel oil and marine diesel. According to the estimates cited in the source, it generates approximately 2-3% of global CO2 emissions. The development of the rules is therefore being monitored by Swiss suppliers that work with the sector.
The process was slowed by opposition from, among others, Saudi Arabia, Russia and the United States. After an initial postponement in October 2025, the decision was postponed again in early September 2026, this time until December.
### Signals from Swiss companies
At the end of August, Accelleron, an Aargau-based turbocharger manufacturer, reported a setback in its annual outlook. The company explained that the postponement of the IMO net-zero regulatory framework had reduced short-term demand. CEO Daniel Bischofberger told the AWP news agency that he did not expect any changes in the short term.
According to Accelleron, operators of smaller and more economical ships invest little in sustainable propulsion without stronger regulatory pressure. Investments are continuing, however, for large container ships and gas carriers, which are also subject to regional rules and companies' climate targets.
Burckhardt Compression reports a similar effect: after the postponement of the Framework, investment decisions are being influenced more strongly by short-term profitability. The spokesperson for the Winterthur-based manufacturer explained the situation, while the group nevertheless considers the long-term trend toward efficient, low-emission marine propulsion systems to be confirmed. For ABB, customer activities are following the normal course of business, while the discussion is broadening from decarbonization to energy efficiency. The three groups agree on the need for greater predictability, stability and clarity regarding future rules; attention is now focused on the decision expected in December. ## What it means for Switzerland
The source focuses on Swiss suppliers and does not describe procedures for families or workers. The impact described is indirect but concrete: greater regulatory uncertainty changes when shipping operators decide to invest and is reflected in Swiss suppliers. The difference between segments and groups is the point to follow.
### A market divided by type of ship
| Segment or group | Signal in the source | | --- | --- | | Smaller and more economical ships | Reduced investment in sustainable propulsion systems without greater regulatory pressure | | Large container ships and LNG carriers | Investments continue due to regional rules and climate targets | | Accelleron | Short-term demand reduced after the postponement | | Burckhardt Compression | Greater weight given to short-term profitability | | ABB | Customer activity normal; discussion also includes energy efficiency |
The table shows why a postponement does not amount to a uniform stop. For smaller and more economical ships, the absence of greater regulatory pressure translates into reduced investment in sustainable propulsion systems. For large container ships and LNG carriers, however, investments continue partly as a result of regional rules and companies' climate targets. The same regulatory phase can therefore create different pressures within the Swiss supply chain.
The case of Burckhardt Compression adds a second criterion: immediate profitability carries more weight in investment decisions. This is a different reading from ABB's, which describes customer activity as normal and notes that the discussion is expanding to energy efficiency. Accelleron, on the other hand, reports an impact already visible in short-term demand. The comparison does not make it possible to determine which company will achieve the best result: the source provides no data on orders, revenue, employment, wages or investments in francs.
The useful point of comparison for a reader is not to ask whether the transition has been abandoned. For Burckhardt Compression, the source says the opposite in the long term: the trend toward efficient, low-emission systems remains confirmed. The issue is the investment timetable and the different responses of customers to regulatory pressure. The December decision will therefore be the next reference point for the sector. Those who want to explore the corporate side can consult the aziende che assumono, while to separate the industrial impact from everyday expenses they can use the costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the December decision
For a Swiss reader, the most solid approach is to turn the postponement into a sequence of checks. The following procedure uses the elements that emerged in the dossier and helps avoid confusing the long-term objective with the immediate question.
### 1. Set the deadline
Consider December the next checkpoint. The timeline to note is: draft approved in April 2025; first postponement in October 2025; new delay announced at the beginning of September 2026. This reference serves to distinguish what has already been approved in draft form from what remains pending.
### 2. Identify the segment
When a new update comes out, ask yourself whether it concerns operators of smaller, more economical ships or large container ships and LNG carriers. In the first case, the source describes limited investment in the absence of regulatory pressure; in the second, it reports that investment is continuing because of regional regulations and companies' climate objectives. This distinction avoids applying the same assessment to the entire maritime transport sector.
### 3. Separate the short and long term
For Accelleron, the postponement reduced short-term demand; for Burckhardt Compression, decisions are more closely tied to immediate profitability. In the long term, however, Burckhardt considers the trend toward efficient, low-emission propulsion to be confirmed. ABB, for its part, reports normal customer activity and growing attention to energy efficiency. The comparison must therefore be updated without seeking a single label for everyone.
### 4. Assess what is missing
Do not attribute effects to the postponement that the text does not measure. The source does not indicate changes in wages, jobs, prices, taxes or the costs faced by Swiss households. If the next update does not add these data, the national impact will remain legible mainly through Swiss suppliers and their industrial prospects, not through a figure applicable to every resident.

item.description: Service available Mon‑Fri 9‑17 at 091 811 30 20, doctor called back within 30 minutes, one-year trial with approximately 800 calls per year.

## In brief - Pronto Consulto is launched in the Mendrisiotto and Basso Ceresio - A doctor calls back within 30 minutes - Service available Monday to Friday, from 9 to 17 - The pilot project lasts one year
## Key facts - Service and area → Pronto Consulto in the Mendrisiotto and Basso Ceresio - Doctor callback → within 30 minutes - Initial availability → Monday-Friday, 9-17 - Number → 091 811 30 20 - Pilot project and estimates → one year; approximately 800 calls per year; possible reduction of 15%
In the Mendrisiotto and Basso Ceresio, Pronto Consulto, a new telephone service designed for people who have a health problem and do not know whether an urgent assessment is necessary, has been launched. The project is presented as a point of guidance between managing the situation at home, waiting to see one's family doctor, the emergency department and intervention by the Servizio Autoambulanza.
The central element is a callback from a hospital doctor: after the telephone call, the user is contacted within 30 minutes. When appropriate, the assessment can also take place via video call. The doctor considers the situation and indicates which course to follow, without Pronto Consulto replacing 144, the emergency department or the family doctor.
The symptoms mentioned include minor injuries, musculoskeletal problems, minor wounds, non-serious breathing problems and general symptoms such as moderate fever and malaise. The list describes cases that may benefit from guidance; the decision on the course of action remains linked to the doctor's assessment.
The service is recognized by health insurance funds, an element indicated in the presentation of the project. The topic can be explored further in the tool dedicated to health insurance funds, without confusing this telephone guidance service with a replacement for urgent care.
### Why the project was created
The initiative is driven by growing pressure on healthcare services, especially the emergency department and ambulance services. These facilities also handle situations that do not require an urgent response. The estimates considered by the promoters indicate that approximately 20% of the cases handled by the two services could be managed through less urgent means.
The project also includes ambulance requests that Centrale Ticino Soccorso classifies as non-urgent. In these situations, a pre-hospital clinical specialist from the Servizio Autoambulanza may be sent to the scene for an initial assessment, without immediately mobilizing a full crew.
At the outset, Pronto Consulto will be available Monday to Friday, from 9 to 17, at 091 811 30 20. The estimated capacity is approximately 800 calls per year and the possible reduction in the workload on the services involved is 15%. The pilot project will last one year: its results will be used to assess the effectiveness of the model, introduce any necessary adjustments and decide whether to make it permanent. ## The path between doubt and care
The practical value of Pronto Consulto lies in placing a medical assessment before the decision about where to seek care. For those who are not healthcare professionals, recognizing the seriousness of a disorder is not always simple: the emergency department or an ambulance may therefore seem like the safest choice. The phone call introduces an intermediate step, with a doctor tasked with directing the case toward the appropriate level of care.
This logic does not produce a single outcome for every call. The assessment may stop at home management, involve waiting for the attending physician, or direct the patient to the emergency department or Servizio Autoambulanza. The table summarizes the pathways described by the project.
| Situation | Possible guidance | |---|---| | Problem manageable at home | Home management | | Need to wait | Attending physician | | Urgent assessment | Emergency department or ambulance | | Non-urgent ambulance request | Possible dispatch of a specialist |
For citizens, the promoters indicate concrete effects: fewer journeys and shorter waiting times and, when a less burdensome form of care is appropriate, lower costs. The stated objective is to offer care commensurate with the individual patient's needs. To explore the topic of costo della vita in Svizzera, this is the economic impact explicitly linked to the project.
The handling of ambulance requests also changes level. If Centrale Ticino Soccorso classifies it as non-urgent, a pre-hospital clinical specialist may arrive at the scene for an initial assessment, without immediately mobilizing a full team. With the support of the doctor from Pronto Consulto, the specialist can direct the patient to the attending physician or another service. The report to the attending physician supports continuity of care and makes it possible, if necessary, to arrange further examinations.
### A precise scope
The project is intended for citizens of the Mendrisiotto and Basso Ceresio and for requests in which it is unclear whether an urgent assessment is needed. It does not present itself as a substitute for 144, the emergency department or the attending physician. The new channel aims to improve coordination between services: it guides the patient and seeks to keep emergency facilities more available for those who need them, in line with the stated objective.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## The procedure for using Pronto Consulto
For anyone with a health problem who does not know whether an urgent assessment is needed, the process begins with a phone call and continues with medical guidance. The steps indicated in the trial are concrete.
### 1. Call during the indicated hours
During the initial phase, the number is 091 811 30 20. It is available Monday to Friday, from 9 to 17. The service is intended for residents of Mendrisiotto and Basso Ceresio; the trial will last one year.
### 2. Wait for the call back
After the phone call, a hospital doctor contacts the user again within 30 minutes. When appropriate, the assessment can also take place via video call. The doctor helps determine whether the problem can be managed at home, whether the patient can wait to see their primary care physician, or whether they need to go to the Emergency Department or activate the Ambulance Service.
### 3. Follow the guidance received
The guidance does not replace 144, the Emergency Department or the primary care physician. If the doctor recommends managing the situation at home or waiting to see the primary care physician, the suggested course remains in place; if the doctor recommends an urgent assessment, the patient is directed to the corresponding service.
### 4. Handle a non-urgent ambulance request
If Centrale Ticino Soccorso classifies an ambulance request as non-urgent, a pre-hospital clinical specialist may be sent for an initial assessment, without immediately mobilizing a full team. With the support of the Pronto Consulto doctor, the specialist can identify the most suitable solution.
### 5. Maintain the connection
If urgent care is not needed, the patient is referred to the primary care physician or another suitable service. The primary care physician is sent a report of the assessment, ensuring continuity of care and arranging, if necessary, further tests.
The sequence is therefore clearly defined: the request reaches the service, the doctor assesses the situation, the patient receives guidance and the primary care physician is involved when urgent care is not needed. Pronto Consulto remains a link between services, not a replacement for them.

## Key facts - What → regularly switching basic insurer - First switch → 563 francs per year on average - Further switch → 383 francs per year on average - 2027 premiums → announcement expected tomorrow - Analysis → switches over the past four years among customers with supplementary insurance
A few hours before the publication of the new premiums for 2027, whose announcement is expected tomorrow, Axa released an analysis this morning of the potential savings. According to the study, regularly switching insurer for mandatory basic insurance is more worthwhile in the long term than remaining with the same health insurer for a long time.
The research comes as the study forecasts a substantial increase for next year as well. The issue highlighted by Axa is the relationship between the first switch and the changes that follow, not only the initial choice of insurer.
With the first switch, policyholders save an average of 563 francs per year. In the event of a further switch, the indicated average saving is 383 francs per year. The figure is lower than that of the first switch, but the study still considers regularly switching worthwhile in the long term.
> «Many policyholders believe that after a first switch, the potential for savings is practically exhausted», said Alexandra Gmür, head of health insurance provision at Axa, quoted in the statement released this morning.
### Scope of the survey
The Keystone-ATS report situates the analysis in the hours preceding the publication of the 2027 premiums. The document, released by Axa, accompanies the wait for tomorrow's expected announcement with an estimate of the potential of repeated switches.
To conduct the study, Axa examined all switches in basic insurance made over the past four years by customers who also had supplementary insurance. The stated scope therefore includes both the first switch and subsequent ones, according to the distinction adopted to calculate the two average savings.
The group also specifies that it does not directly offer basic insurance. The analysis is thus presented as an assessment of the savings potential observed in the switches considered, and not as a proposal for an Axa basic insurance product.
For those who keep the same insurer for a long time, the source therefore points to possible savings left on the table; for those who have already switched, the review is not described as concluded. These are the two situations that Axa compares on the eve of the new announcement. ## Put the comparison in your calendar
Axa recommends that policyholders note the comparison of premiums in their calendar every year. The immediate reference is the publication of the premiums for 2027, scheduled for tomorrow: the appointment can become the moment to reopen the comparison, without considering the savings exhausted after a single choice.
### The operational sequence
1. Mark an annual time in your calendar dedicated to comparing premiums, as suggested by Axa. 2. When the new 2027 premiums are published, check the compulsory basic insurance again and the possibility of changing insurer. 3. Include in the same comparison the savings-oriented insurance models indicated in the source: family doctor, telemedicine and HMO. 4. Also assess alternative deductibles, without stopping at the name of the health insurer alone.
The first step should not be treated as a conclusive check. The same analysis also takes subsequent changes into consideration and links regular checking to long-term cost-effectiveness. The procedure indicated is therefore an annual habit, to be reopened when the new premium data arrive.
The scope of the study should be kept in mind when reading the results: Axa examined the changes made over the last four years by customers who also had supplementary insurance. The group also clarifies that it does not directly offer basic insurance. The reported figures therefore describe the analysis of the changes considered by Axa.
In the comparison, basic coverage remains the starting point. The alternatives mentioned concern the insurance model and the deductible; these are the items that the recommendation invites one to reconsider every year together with the premium. item.title: Switzerland a digital leader but lagging behind in cyber defense
item.description: Switzerland leads digital competitiveness with 100/100, but is only 31st out of 66 for cyber preparedness (5,32/10); attacks have increased by 35% and 7 incidents have been recorded in the past year.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Swiss digital competitiveness: 100/100 - Cyber threat preparedness: 31st place out of 66 - Cyberattacks on organizations: +35% in one year - Seven attacks or political incidents in the past year
## Key facts
- Study → Abilene Academy - Countries analyzed → 66 - Switzerland’s digital competitiveness → 100/100 - Cyber threat preparedness → 5,32/10 - Position in preparedness → 31st place
## Digital leadership and the weak point
ZURICH - Switzerland leads the digital competitiveness ranking, but remains only in 31st place out of 66 when the metric changes and concerns preparedness to counter cyber threats. This is the paradox highlighted by a new international study conducted by Abilene Academy, an organization specializing in governance, risk and compliance.
The digital score is 100/100. In this ranking, Switzerland comes ahead of the United States, Sweden, Denmark and the Netherlands, which score 99,29, 95,42, 97,23 and 96,82 respectively. In terms of response to cyber threats, however, the result falls to 5,32 out of 10. The gap between the two figures is at the heart of the research: the drive for innovation does not automatically correspond to an equivalent defensive capacity.
### The attack data
According to the study, in the past year Swiss organizations recorded 7 cyberattacks or political incidents. The report indicates 0,0777 incidents per 100.000 inhabitants, a figure higher than that recorded in France (0,0644), Germany (0,0478) and Italy (0,0255). The source also reports that attacks against Swiss organizations increased by 35% in one year: the comparison therefore concerns not only a position in the ranking, but also the evolution of the phenomenon.
The European comparison makes the gap even more pronounced. France, despite having 81,91 points in digital competitiveness, ranks 14th in preparedness. Germany reaches 84,25 points in competitiveness and 6,45 in the overall score; Italy totals 6,32. Thus Switzerland retains the best digital ecosystem among the major European economies, but the lowest score for cybersecurity preparedness.
Globally, Singapore leads the preparedness ranking with 8,53 out of 10, followed by the United Arab Emirates, Finland, Saudi Arabia and the United States. Switzerland remains mid-table for resilience to cyber threats. Henri Haenni, general director of Abilene Academy, sums up the distinction in one sentence:
> «being at the forefront of digitalization is not enough to guarantee an economy’s resilience to cyber threats».
Haenni adds that cybersecurity must be integrated into governance and decision-making processes at all levels. For Switzerland, the priority identified by the study is to develop digital risk management alongside technological capabilities. Alexis Hirschhorn, CEO of ACUNA GRC, describes the same gap between world-class infrastructure and risk management that is not always aligned. The message of the study is therefore clear: digital leadership alone does not guarantee resilience. ## The gap between technology and resilience
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the most useful figure is not only digital leadership, but the separation between two capabilities that the study keeps distinct: innovating and withstanding cyber threats. The score of 100/100 measures digital competitiveness; the 5,32 out of 10, on the other hand, measures preparedness to counter cyber threats. They are not two ways of saying the same thing. The research shows that an advanced technological ecosystem does not automatically produce an equally ready response to incidents.
### Comparison as a lens for interpretation
Comparison with neighboring countries avoids an overly simple explanation. France scores 81,91 points in digital competitiveness, therefore less than Switzerland, but ranks 14th in preparedness. Germany reaches 84,25 points and an overall score of 6,45; Italy scores 6,32. The rankings suggest that digital competitiveness and cyber resilience must be assessed separately. Looking only at the strength of the digital ecosystem is not enough to understand how ready an economy is to respond.
For a Swiss organization finding itself in the situation described, the practical consequence is a change in priorities. Investing in security technologies may be part of the response, but according to Alexis Hirschhorn, it does not by itself close the gap. Governance must become operational and must enter into daily decisions, beyond the logic of the annual audit. Risk management thus becomes a process responsibility, not an isolated control.
Henri Haenni takes the same reasoning beyond the IT department alone. As cyber threats increase and become more sophisticated, he says, cybersecurity must be integrated into governance and decision-making processes at all levels. For those working in a Swiss organization, the concrete point is to understand whether the ability to respond to incidents is considered a function of the organization as a whole or merely a technical issue. The study points toward the former interpretation.
This perspective is also useful to those examining the aziende che assumono or looking in the annunci di lavoro for the weight of digital skills: competitiveness and resilience do not coincide. They are two dimensions of the Swiss system that the research encourages us not to confuse.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Five steps for translating the study’s message
The operational message of the research can be translated into five steps for an organization that wants to align its digital level with its defense capability. These are governance steps, not a catalog of technologies: this is the distinction outlined by Abilene Academy and the two executives cited.
1. Separate the two measures. Assess digital competitiveness on the one hand and readiness to counter threats on the other; a result of 100/100 does not replace 5,32 out of 10. 2. Bring risk into governance. Cybersecurity should not be left solely to the IT department: it must be integrated into decision-making processes at all levels. 3. Make governance operational. The reference point is not only the annual audit; risk management must become part of everyday decisions. 4. Align management and technology. Digital risk management must evolve in step with technological capabilities; investing in new security technologies alone does not close the gap. 5. Build response capability. Resilience requires sound risk management and the ability to respond to incidents; according to Haenni, it is acquired through experience and cannot be decreed.
### The question to bring into decision-making
Applied to a Swiss context, the sequence starts with a question: is the level of innovation progressing alongside digital risk management? If the answer is not aligned, the problem identified by the research cannot be solved by proclaiming technological primacy. It must be addressed in decision-making processes and in the ability to respond to incidents.
For those who live or work in the country, the most concrete action is therefore to view cybersecurity as a governance issue, not as a subject confined to IT. The criterion proposed by the study can be verified in organizational practice: does risk enter everyday decisions or does it appear only in the annual audit? The answer makes it possible to understand whether digital infrastructure is accompanied by risk management that is up to the task, without confusing a single investment with resilience.
The priority indicated for Switzerland remains to make digital risk management evolve in step with technological capabilities. This is a direction that carries even greater weight as threats increase and become more sophisticated. ## In brief - 70% rejected the neutrality initiative - The no vote strengthens the position of the Federal Council - The press speaks of a defeat for Christoph Blocher - Blocher's campaign cost almost 4 million francs
- Subject → neutrality initiative - Outcome → 70% opposed - Main figure → Christoph Blocher - Financing → almost 4 million francs - Political effect → endorsement of the policy of Parliament and the Executive
The 70% of no votes recorded at the polls yesterday is being read by the Swiss media as the chronicle of a foretold defeat. The clear rejection strengthens the position of the Federal Council and personally hits Christoph Blocher.
### The newspapers' reading
> «The 70% of no votes is an unappealable verdict for those who were aiming for rigid neutrality for its own sake,» writes Corriere del Ticino.
The daily interprets the result as an endorsement of the policy of Parliament and the Executive and believes that the initiative has closed every serious avenue for a revival. La Regione reaches a similar assessment: the vote prevents neutrality from being turned into a dogma and returns it to the role of an instrument of Swiss foreign policy, to be used flexibly according to global circumstances.
NZZ also speaks of an unappealable result. The Zurich daily recalls that Blocher's initiative, financed with almost 4 million francs, would not have stood a chance from the outset.
For the Swiss-German publications of the Tamedia group, the defeat is personal: the former democentrist Federal Councillor would not even have convinced his own party. Blick reads the vote as a gradual transition away from the patriarch of the UDC. According to the newspaper, the next dossier will be that of the European Union and will likely be entrusted to Magdalena Martullo-Blocher.
La Liberté speaks of a thrashing inflicted by the people and a signal to Blocher; Le Temps emphasizes that his commitment and the millions he personally spent were not enough. The publications of the ESH group recall that a popular majority is more difficult to buy than posters and advertisements.
Le Temps finally links the no vote to the UDC's third defeat of the year and sees in it a resounding yes to the way the Federal Council applies neutrality: according to the newspaper, it is the first time that this approach has received popular endorsement on such a scale. The most concrete issue concerns the way neutrality is defined and used. For the Federal Council, Parliament and the Executive, the result therefore represents an endorsement of the policy pursued.
### Before and after the vote

The comparison shows the scope for discussion after the vote. It is not merely a matter of determining whether neutrality should remain an important principle, but of deciding how to employ it when circumstances in the world change. The Regione's reading insists precisely on this point: a means must be usable with the necessary flexibility, without becoming a dogma. This is the most concrete political consequence described by the press review.
The national dimension also emerges from the comparison between the newspapers. The Ticino newspapers speak of an unequivocal verdict and of the closing of any possibility of relaunching the initiative. The NZZ emphasizes the lack of any chance from the outset. item.title: Massimo Balena: Ticino farmer in the Swiss calendar
item.description: The 29-year-old from Bellinzona recounts the apprenticeship in German, the closure of the company with 650 hens, and the intensive work of up to 15 hours a day.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Massimo Balena is 29 years old and is originally from Bellinzona. - She is the Ticino face of the Swiss Farmers' Calendar. - Apprenticeship: Bergün, Jenins and Davos, a different company every year. - His farm of 650 hens has been closed.
## Key Facts - Person → Massimo Balena - Age → 29 years - Origin → Bellinzona - Calendar → Swiss Farmers' Calendar - Apprenticeship → Bergün, Jenins and Davos - Farm → 650 hens - Stream → about 2 meters from the stable - Haymaking → up to 15 hours per day
Massimo Balena, a 29-year-old native of Bellinzona, is the Ticino face of the Swiss Farmers' Calendar. His presence in the calendar was born from an inscription made by his girlfriend, almost for fun. For him, accustomed to a daily life between animals and agricultural rhythms, putting himself in front of a photographer meant entering a new environment.
At first he feared that people who know him would joke about participation. In the workplace there were jokes, but in a light atmosphere. During the shots, the tension decreased, to the point of leaving room for greater spontaneity. He said he was almost proud of the result: he is a shy person, but he chose to put his face to it and get involved.
> "He signed me up and we said: 'let's see what happens'. If they take me well, if they don't take me I have nothing to lose."
### From grandmother to career path
Massimo's agricultural story began away from the spotlight and without a peasant tradition behind him. The first contact came at his grandmother's holiday home in Campoblenio, when he was seven, eight or nine years old: he went from one stable to another to see how it worked and helped as much as he could. Interest grew when his brother chose an agricultural background.
Hence the decision to do the apprenticeship away from Ticino: Bergün the first year, Jenins the second and Davos the last. Changing companies every year served, in his experience, to learn more. School and work were in German, and the first year was quite hard. The path therefore required both mobility and linguistic adaptation.
He appreciates the days outdoors and the relationship with the animals, to whom he tries to ensure the best possible well-being. He also appreciates the fact that the climate conditions the programs: during haymaking, the rain can quickly change plans. This variability, in his eyes, makes the activity freer and more flexible than the office routine. For those who look at the sector as a possible outlet, his path offers a reference to consult the annunci di lavoro, without separating the professional choice from the concrete conditions of the job. ## Why the profession remains difficult
The most concrete aspect of the account concerns the relationship between regulations, working hours and economic appeal. Massimo describes an agricultural policy facing major difficulties: he says that every year a different, more complicated law comes along, and that those who work have to adapt. In his case, this adaptation had a clear outcome: the closure of the small farm with 650 hens.
### Rules, working hours and the image of the profession
According to the account, the barn was located next to a stream, about two meters away. He was told that the chickens' droppings were polluting it. The barn had been there for more than two or three hundred years, the stream had always run in the same place and the chickens were raised outdoors, in full view of everyone. For years, he adds, cows and horses had also been kept in the area. Then the arrival of a new person in the Canton led to a different decision. In his account, the practical consequence was the closure of the operation.
The second element is time. In summer, during haymaking, one can work as many as 15 hours a day, from morning to evening and from Monday to Sunday. Massimo identifies agriculture as the only sector in which, in his view, one can work more than 55 hours a week and claims that every farmer works more than 60 or 65. Few vacation periods and not-very-high earnings make the profession less attractive to young people. Since the source does not provide a figure, the comparison with busta paga svizzera should be read as a personal tool, not as a sector average.
The third element is image. In Kostlers, where he lives today, Massimo sees young people rejecting agriculture even though they come from families active in the sector. In Bellinzona, as a boy, he instead perceived it as a distant world and encountered stereotypes when he announced to his classmates that he had chosen an apprenticeship. The distance between actual work and its social representation thus becomes another obstacle to entry.

Massimo's story can become a checklist for anyone considering an apprenticeship or agricultural activity. It is not an administrative procedure valid for everyone: it is a sequence of questions drawn from the conditions he describes. It serves to separate the idea of working outdoors from daily constraints.
### Five checks before choosing
1. Verify your relationship with animals and outdoor work. Massimo speaks of affection for animals and the responsibility of ensuring their well-being. For anyone considering the sector, this is the daily aspect to put first.
2. Accept the variability of the weather and working hours. Haymaking can be affected by rain, while summer may require long days. The flexibility Massimo prefers to office routine must be assessed together with the willingness to change plans.
3. View the apprenticeship as a mobile path. In his case, it took place in different locations, with a different company each year so he could learn more. School and work were in German, and the first year was difficult: travel and language are part of the choice described.
4. Examine the relationship between the operation and the environment. The closure of his chicken operation was linked to the stream near the stable. The case suggests clarifying in advance the conditions concerning the place where one works, without taking for granted that a historical situation will remain unchanged.
5. Assess economic and personal sustainability. The story speaks of few vacation periods and not particularly high earnings, as well as weeks that can exceed 55 hours and, according to Massimo, reach more than 60 or 65. These are factors to compare with your own budget.

### The Federal Council's interpretation
Ignazio Cassis, federal councillor and head of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA), ruled out the possibility that the no vote on the neutrality proposal represented an abandonment of the principle.
> «This result is not a vote against neutrality. Switzerland was neutral yesterday, is neutral today and will remain so in the future».
For the Federal Council, the practice of the past 180 years has proven valid because it has not treated neutrality rigidly. Cassis described periods that were more restrictive and others that were more open to cooperation, always with the same objective: ensuring the country's security and preventing Switzerland from becoming involved in a war.
The federal councillor pointed to 2022, after Russia's attack on Ukraine, as the case that makes this approach concrete. According to his explanation, the Federal Council reacted because the attack by a larger country against a smaller one constituted a decisive violation of international law. The political rule invoked is therefore to assess the situation as it is.
Following Cassis, Guy Parmelin commented on the no vote on the food initiative. The President of the Confederation acknowledged the importance of agricultural issues and self-sufficiency, arguing that Switzerland must be able to guarantee it for future generations as well.
